“University in Germany is completely free”

The truth: Most places: no tuition, but a semester contribution. No tuition at most universities, but a contribution every semester: FU Berlin €376.80, Münster €369.50 (winter 2026/27). Rent and living costs are separate.

Source: fu-berlin.de, uni-muenster.de (checked November 2026). Confirm on the official page before you apply.

Minimum English requirement in Seattle: IELTS 6.0

University of Washington asks first-years for IELTS 6.0 or TOEFL 76 (new scale 4.0). The deadline is 15 November; test by 31 December at the latest. Meeting the minimum does not mean admission. The page does not state a year.

Source: admit.washington.edu (checked November 2026). Confirm on the official page before you apply.

info.text:
uni-assist and VPD: the way to apply to some German universities

1. Check the university: Not every university uses uni-assist. The university tells you whether it asks for a VPD (pre-assessment document).
2. Open a My assist account: Create your online application and upload your diploma and transcript. The university tells you which documents you need.
3. Pay the fee: First program €75, each extra one in the same semester €30. Payment requests only come through the uni-assist portal.
4. Wait for the VPD: Processing usually takes 4 to 6 weeks. Apply at least 8 weeks before the deadline. A VPD is valid for one year.
5. Upload to the university: Send the VPD and your other documents to the university's own portal, before its own deadline.

Some universities take applications directly; at others, uni-assist forwards them. The fee applies again each semester.

Source: uni-assist.de (checked November 2026). Confirm on the official page before you apply.

No tuition on most programs at LMU

LMU has charged no tuition since winter 2013/14; you pay a semester contribution. Some special master's programs do charge fees. Munich's student services organization sets the contribution amount. Living costs are separate.

Source: lmu.de (checked November 2026). Confirm on the official page before you apply.
